title: Errors & correction
description: 55 questions: the existing 40 plus 15 new Moderate–Hard items. Select Moderate–Hard for the new sets with close alternatives and full-context checks. Difficulty is a reviewed training target, not an independently calibrated exam rating.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar
source.note: Source references describe formats only; all sentences, options and explanations in this chapter are newly authored.

collocations: within the stipulated period / a stipulated condition
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The borrower submitted the documents within the stipulated period.

questions.prompt: The list of discrepancies [have been sent] to the auditor.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: List, not discrepancies, controls the verb.
explanation.rule: A singular head noun takes has; perfect passive is has been + past participle.
explanation.model: The list of discrepancies has been sent to the auditor.

rejects.reason: Have disagrees with singular list; being also does not form the required perfect passive.
After been, the passive needs the past participle sent.
The head noun list is singular, so were does not agree.
Discrepancies is inside of the phrase; the subject head is list.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: Every applicant [must submits] an identity document.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Must already carries the modal function.
explanation.rule: Use modal + base verb, irrespective of whether the subject is singular.
explanation.model: Every applicant must submit an identity document.

rejects.reason: A modal takes the base form, not the past participle.
An -ing form cannot directly follow must here.
Do not insert to after the modal must.
The singular applicant does not add -s to a verb after must.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The analyst [suggested to revise] the tentative estimate.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: The action after suggested is revising.
explanation.rule: Use suggest + -ing, or suggest that + clause; only the -ing construction is offered.
explanation.model: The analyst suggested revising the tentative estimate.

rejects.reason: A bare verb cannot be the direct complement in this construction.
Suggest does not require for before this action complement.
To revising does not repair the complement.
Suggest + to-infinitive is not the required pattern here.

questions.prompt: The revised policy [aims to reduce delays and improving] accountability.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.
options: aims to reducing delays and improve
aims to reduced delays and improved
aims to reduce delays and improve
questions.answer: aims to reduce delays and improve

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: The two intended actions share aims to.
explanation.rule: Coordinate reduce and improve under the same to.
explanation.model: The revised policy aims to reduce delays and improve accountability.

rejects.option: aims to reducing delays and improve
rejects.reason: Aims to here takes an infinitive, not reducing.
Aims needs to before the infinitive and parallel verb forms.

rejects.option: aims to reduced delays and improved

Reduce and improving are not parallel in this shared infinitive structure.

questions.prompt: The bank has [fewer liquidity than] it needs for immediate withdrawals.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Liquidity names an amount, not a count of objects.
explanation.rule: Use less with an uncountable amount and than for this comparison.
explanation.model: The bank has less liquidity than it needs for immediate withdrawals.

rejects.reason: Few requires plural count nouns and does not form this comparison.
The comparative pairing and normal quantifier are wrong here.
Liquidity is uncountable in this cash-availability sense.
Fewer counts separate items; liquidity here is an amount.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The manager is responsible [for verify] the collateral documents.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Responsible for introduces the duty.
explanation.rule: Use responsible for + noun or -ing form.
explanation.model: The manager is responsible for verifying the collateral documents.

rejects.reason: Responsible is followed by for in this construction.
A past participle cannot name the action after for here.
A to-infinitive cannot directly follow this preposition.
The verb after for must take an -ing form here.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The team has [made considerable progress] in reconciling the accounts.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Has made and uncountable progress already fit.
explanation.rule: Do not change an accurate sentence just because an error is expected.
explanation.model: The team has made considerable progress in reconciling the accounts.

rejects.reason: Progress is uncountable in this sense.
The natural construction is make progress, without a.
Has needs the past participle made.
Progress is a noun and needs the adjective considerable.

questions.prompt: The officer asked [whether the records were complete].
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: The question is embedded after asked.
explanation.rule: Use whether + subject + verb in an indirect yes/no question.
explanation.model: The officer asked whether the records were complete.

rejects.reason: An embedded question uses statement word order.
That does not introduce this yes/no indirect question.
Plural records requires were.
Do-support does not belong in this embedded question and changes the structure.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The committee decided [to defer the vote until] the audit was complete.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Completion of the audit marks the end of the waiting period.
explanation.rule: Decide to do something; until introduces the endpoint.
explanation.model: The committee decided to defer the vote until the audit was complete.

rejects.reason: Decided takes a to-infinitive in this construction.
To must be followed by base defer.
Unless changes the intended endpoint into an exception condition.
By cannot introduce the finite clause the audit was complete here.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The report describes the measures [taken to mitigate] operational risk.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: The measures were taken; their purpose was mitigation.
explanation.rule: Taken is a reduced passive relative clause; to mitigate expresses purpose.
explanation.model: The report describes the measures taken to mitigate operational risk.

rejects.reason: Measures needs a passive modifier, not active took.
Purpose to takes base mitigate.
This would make the measures the agents doing the taking.
For cannot be followed directly by base mitigate here.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The association looks forward [to receive] a conclusive response.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Look forward to is the complete expression.
explanation.rule: Use look forward to + noun/-ing, unlike ordinary want to + base verb.
explanation.model: The association looks forward to receiving a conclusive response.

rejects.reason: The fixed expression is look forward to.
The prepositional to needs an -ing action complement here.
Dropping to breaks the expression.
This to is a preposition, not an infinitive marker.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: The officer prevented the applicant [from submit] an incomplete form.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: The application was stopped before submission.
explanation.rule: Use prevent + person + from + -ing.
explanation.model: The officer prevented the applicant from submitting an incomplete form.

rejects.reason: Prevent someone from doing something is the required construction.
The preposition from requires the action noun form submitting here.
For would suggest a reason, not the prevented action.
Base submit cannot directly follow from in this pattern.

questions.prompt: Had the discrepancy been detected earlier, the bank [would avoid] the loss last month.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Had ... been detected and last month refer to an unreal past event.
explanation.rule: In this past counterfactual, use had + participle and would have + participle.
explanation.model: Had the discrepancy been detected earlier, the bank would have avoided the loss last month.

rejects.reason: Will does not express this unreal past result.
A modal takes have, not had.
This lacks the result modal and correct participle.
Last month and had been detected make this a past counterfactual.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: Rarely [the panel has encountered] such a tenuous argument.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: Rarely opens the clause.
explanation.rule: With fronted rarely, move the auxiliary before the subject: has the panel encountered.
explanation.model: Rarely has the panel encountered such a tenuous argument.

rejects.reason: This misses inversion and disagrees with singular panel as used here.
Inversion places the subject between auxiliary and main verb.
Did requires base encounter.
Fronted restrictive rarely requires subject–auxiliary inversion here.

formatReferences: Mains Checklist 53: PDF pp2–5, combined grammar

questions.prompt: No sooner [had the moratorium ended when] repayments resumed.
questions.instructions: Replace only the phrase in square brackets. Select No change required if it is already correct.

explanation.relationship: Grammar: preserve the meaning while repairing the marked phrase
explanation.clue: No sooner is the fixed opening.
explanation.rule: Use no sooner had + subject + participle + than + following event.
explanation.model: No sooner had the moratorium ended than repayments resumed.

rejects.reason: Fronted no sooner requires inversion.
Had takes past participle ended.
The paired conjunction is than, not then.
No sooner pairs with than; hardly/scarcely commonly pair with when.
